story.title: Papa Knows a Lot, but Mamma Knows Everything
paragraphs_en: “Wake up! Deepu, wake up!” yelled Deepika’s mother. “It’s a Sunday morning and I have to rush to the weekly village market to fetch the fresh vegetables and fruits.” Deepika woke up, rubbing her eyes and bid goodbye to her mother.
Just then, Deepika heard a loud sound coming from their backyard, “Ouch!! Shoo shoo!” She rushed to see what was going on. Her father was screaming at someone.

"Go away, why’re you after my life, you black crow? For God's sake, let me fill some water from the well! I don't know from where out of the blue this annoying creature came and started pecking me hard on my head. Ouch ouch!!!" bawled Deepika's father. Shoo!! Stop! Shoo!

“Ugh! Ouch!” screamed Deepika, “You stupid cro…ouch! It’s hitting me too!" Hearing all the clutter, their neighbour, Lakshmi came out with her greedy dog, Lalu. “What’s the noise all abou… ouch! Stop you crow! Oh..so this is the root cause of the problem!” realized Lakshmi. “The crow is thirsty. I'll get a bucket of water.” But the crow didn’t care. Rather, Deepika tripped over the bucket and converted the backyard into a small pond! Ouch! Ouch! Dharaam!!!

“Go and bring your dadi, Deepu!” said Deepika’s father. Soon Deepika got her granny on her wheelchair. She looked at the crow suspiciously and said, “Hmm…I get that now…The crow is none other than my great grandfather, Alokanand. He’s hungry! We must give him his favourite dish, jaggery payasam (an Indian dessert made of milk, rice, and nuts).” She then made a yummy payasam, and placed a huge pot full of it near the well. But the crow didn't even look at it.

H earing the chaos, Bindiya mausi (aunty), who was making rotis (bread) in the kitchen, came with a long and sturdy belan (the bread roller). “What's this noise all abou… ouch! Get away you cruel cro..ouch! Wait… ouch!” she screamed in a shrilled voice, trying to hit the crow with her belan. But the crow escaped.

Deepika’s father then got an idea, “Let me call Bulchul Pandey, my inspector friend.” Bulchul Pandey rushed to rescue them, “What’s the thing my frien…ouch! So this is the thing. Wait… I’ll shoot it with my gun.” But he missed the shot.

“We can scare it b y the scarecrow, which my farmer friend, Ram Khilawan has,” said Deepika’s father. Soon Ram Khilawan came with his scary-looking scarecrow and positioned it near the well. But the crow didn’t even give a damn. It instead chased Ram Khilawan and shooed him away. Hmm! Chala aya mujhey daraane!!!

“Let's feed it with corn. I am sure it will be satisfied then!" claimed Bhulwa, the techie of the village. But that didn’t work too. They were all frustrated by now. Gargle says, "Crows love to eat corn."

Right then, “Deepu..arrey oh Deepu…open the door! Look what I got for you.” called out Deepika’s mother. “Oh..mamma..she came back...I am sure she will solve this problem.” exclaimed Deepika with relief. Then they all told her the entire story before Deepika’s mother could utter a word. “Oh… show me the crow,” appealed Deepika’s mother.

Off they went to see the crow. “Oh… ouch! So this is the… ouch! Wait a minute…She looks worried,” explained Deepika’s mother. She took Deepika's binoculars and looked carefully to see what was there on the roof of their storeroom, next to the well. “It’s a nest! The mother crow is trying to protect its eggs.” she whispered. “And so it’s hitting everyone thinking that we could harm them. We need to just leave them alone for a few days, and things will be fine.”
And Deepika’s mother was right! Deepika remarked with glee, “Papa knows a lot, but mamma knows everything!”
